key_insight: Closure-level accuracy in shock solvers necessitates addressing observability issues and capturing tail-weighted distribution dynamics.
engineering_relevance: Improving the accuracy of fluid dynamics models can lead to better simulations and predictions in various engineering applications.
method: Utilized a positive macro–micro PINN approach for modeling BGK shock waves.
Incorporated a bounded exponential correction to the local Maxwellian distribution.
Validated results against independent discrete-velocity method (DVM) references.
evidence_signal: Shock-tube tests illustrated that joint anchoring of observables improves stabilization of nonequilibrium layers.
watch_item: The model struggles with accurately recovering certain higher-order moments, specifically $R_{xx}^{cl}$, due to tail-weighting effects.
paper_title: Tail observability and fourth-order closure recovery in physics-informed neural networks for Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook normal shocks
